summary: Allow retained SMB3 recovery points to be read when the source share rejects writes. API impact: existing contract (restore and catalog read semantics).

guide.reason: Repository troubleshooting distinguishes a write-denied backup/health check from reading a retained recovery point.

api.reason: No request or response schema changes. Core's existing restore and catalog reads no longer require the SMB3 publication write probe; exact published manual-backup replay without retention can settle from the validated point despite write denial. Policy settlement with pending retention, new backup, delete and health operations still require write access.

roadmap.reason: Corrects a destination outage gate already required by the handover plan.

state.reason: No new durable state; Core continues to own the repository, point and restore record.

verification.method: A controlled disposable SMB3 server-side write denial exposed the restore failure. The focused regression was red before the read path and green after; focused race and serial full Go tests passed. Independent source review found no runtime or safety issue and identified a test assertion gap that was corrected. A clean current-source capability-only Core overlay then restored the protected point while the share denied writes, verified both copied disk markers and exact replay, preserved the five point IDs and source hashes, and recovered write access after the original Samba config was restored. A follow-up exact published-backup retry regression failed before removing the redundant reconciliation write probe and passed afterward, including an absent-point case, under focused race checking.
verification.limits: This proves one mounted SMB3 share with server-side write denial, not a locally read-only CIFS remount or all destination outage profiles. Published manual-backup replay under write denial has source regression coverage only; policy settlement still needs writes to complete retention. Broader faults, signed release and forge CI remain open.
